notes: Homepage nav found /clearance/ -- confirmed this is an editorial LANDING HUB ('Clearance – Up to 50% off' H1, zero product-tile elements on the page), not itself a PLP; excluded per PLP-vs-editorial test. It links to /clearance/all-clearance/ which IS a genuine PLP (hitcount 32 products in 'All clearance') with department children in the site's own nav: accessories, beds-and-bedroom (8), dining-furniture (7), living-furniture (6), sofas-and-armchairs (11). accessories/ was verified byte-for-byte identical in size and hitcount (32, same 'All clearance' page) to the parent -- i.e. the accessories clearance category currently has 0 products and the site falls back to re-serving the parent listing; dropped per the zero-product rule. Children that ARE genuine (8+7+6+11=32) sum EXACTLY to the parent hitcount -- clean match. Also checked /sale/ (redirects to /offers/) which is a generic temporary Special-Buys/offers hub organized by department with no clearance/outlet/final-sale/end-of-line taxonomy language anywhere -- excluded per the Sale-vs-Clearance rule as a generic promotional page, not recorded as a row. Checked /outlet, /clearance-outlet -- 404, no separate outlet tree exists. ACCESS QUIRK (worth flagging for future workers on this site): every direct HTTP request to /clearance/all-clearance/* triggers a forced 302 server-side redirect injecting an 'availableInStore' store-filter based on IP geolocation (curl exit route geolocated to Delhi -> store id 27; a separate WebFetch exit route geolocated to Norwich -> presumably a different store) -- this could NOT be disabled via cookies, spoofed CF-IPCountry/X-Forwarded-For headers, dw_dnt cookies, format=ajax, or the raw SFCC Search-Show/Search-UpdateGrid controllers (all either redirected back to the same friendly URL or errored). However both independently-geolocated fetches returned the IDENTICAL total (32, with the same 8/7/6/11 department breakdown), which gives strong confidence this is the genuine unfiltered clearance catalogue count (clearance/returned stock appears centrally listed regardless of nearest store), not an artificially reduced one -- so it was recorded as a normal (non-flagged) qty rather than null.
